report.summary: Our assessment of 10 Shell environmental claims, with the Annual Report 2025 (published 2026-03-12) as the main source plus two ASA-ruled ads: 5 hold up, 5 are unsubstantiated, 0 misleading. Rulings found: ASA not upheld on a Shell Energy LinkedIn ad (2025-10-01); ASA not upheld on a Shell UK TV ad (2025-04-09, outside the 12-month window, flagged); ASA upheld in part in 2023 (history only); and a New York appellate court on 2026-10-08 upheld dismissal of NYC's greenwashing suit over Shell's V-Power Nitro+ ads, which is not a finding that the claims were true. The main concerns are substantiation of the 2050 net-zero target (2030 target weakened, 2035 target retired, Shell's own caveat that it may not meet the target if society is not net zero), generic 'cleaner' wording, the unranked claim that LNG is the 'biggest contribution' to the energy transition, a design-stage LNG Canada claim that rests on projections, and self-reported low-carbon spend. Several quotes come from the investor-facing Annual Report, so consumer-protection rules are applied as a substantiation yardstick. Shell's own web pages returned only metadata to our fetcher, so those quotes are meta-description text. EU Green Claims Directive (COM(2023)166) is a pending proposal only and is not relied on; Directive 2024/825 applies from 27 Sep 2026. Shell was not approached for a right of reply.

claims.claim: Net-zero emissions energy business by 2050 target
claims.reason: Quote: "We have a target to become a net-zero emissions energy business by 2050, and we are committed to playing our part in helping to decarbonise the global energy system." The available evidence does not support that the target is backed by a detailed, independently verified implementation plan. Shell weakened its 2030 carbon-intensity target and retired its 2035 target, and says it 'may not meet this target' if society is not net zero in 2050. The CEO downplayed the commitment in Feb 2026. The text is investor-facing.
claims.rule: Directive 2024/825 (UCPD Art. 6(2)(d)); CMA Green Claims Code principles 3 and 6

claims.claim: Generic 'cleaner energy solutions' and reducing emissions
claims.reason: Quote: "we are reducing emissions from our operations, and helping our customers transition to cleaner energy solutions." The available evidence does not support the comparative 'cleaner' without a stated baseline. Shell's own report shows about 1,142 Mt CO2e gross emissions, mostly Scope 3, and plans LNG sales growth of 4-5% a year. No regulator has ruled on this wording; the NY appellate court (2026-10-08) rejected NYC's claims over 'cleaner' fuel ads under NYC consumer law, a different jurisdiction and standard.
claims.rule: Directive 2024/825 / UCPD Annex I point 4a (generic claims); CMA Green Claims Code principles 2 and 3

claims.claim: LNG as a lower-carbon alternative to coal
claims.reason: Quote: "It is also a lower-carbon alternative to coal for industry and power, and to diesel and fuel oil for heavy-duty transport and shipping." Our assessment is that this is supported on average: the IEA estimates LNG gives about 25% less lifecycle emissions than coal, with more than 99% of 2024 LNG below coal. The IEA also says a coal-only comparison 'sets the bar too low', and IISD says LNG lifecycle emissions are typically underestimated because of methane leakage.
claims.rule: CMA Green Claims Code principles 1 and 3

claims.claim: LNG as the biggest contribution to the energy transition
claims.reason: Quote: "That is why we believe that supplying LNG will be the biggest contribution we will make to the energy transition over the next decade." The available evidence does not support the ranking; no comparative analysis against Shell's other contributions was found. IISD concludes new LNG is more likely to add to than replace other fuel use, and the IEA warns against coal-only comparisons.
claims.rule: CMA Green Claims Code principles 5 and 6; Directive 2024/825 (UCPD Art. 6(2)(d)) if used in consumer communications

claims.claim: LNG Canada 'among the lowest carbon intensity LNG facilities in the world'
claims.reason: Quote: "it was designed to be among the lowest carbon intensity LNG facilities in the world". The available evidence does not support it as a measured fact: IISD says the widely cited '60% cleaner' figure comes from the project's environmental assessment and rests on projections rather than observed data. IISD also says liquefaction is under 10% of lifecycle emissions, so facility-level intensity says little about the product's full footprint.
claims.rule: CMA Green Claims Code principles 5 and 6; Directive 2024/825 / UCPD Annex I point 4b if repeated to consumers

claims.claim: About 70% of the way to halving Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030
claims.reason: Quote: "By the end of 2025, we had achieved around 70% of our target to halve our Scope 1 and 2 operational emissions by 2030, compared with 2016." The figures are internally consistent (53 Mt in 2025 vs 58 Mt in 2024; about -36% vs 2016) and the report's contents list an independent auditor's report on the sustainability statements. Independent trade coverage repeats the numbers, but this is not independent re-measurement. Part of the fall is attributed to portfolio changes, and Scope 3 (about 1,065 Mt) dwarfs Scope 1+2.
claims.rule: CMA Green Claims Code principles 1 and 3

claims.claim: Delivered $10-15bn investment in low-carbon energy solutions 2023-2025
claims.reason: Quote: "At our Capital Markets Day 2023, we said we would invest $10--15 billion in low-carbon energy solutions between 2023 and 2025, which we have delivered on." (double hyphen is a rendering artefact of the mirror copy). Insufficient public evidence of independent verification: S&P Global repeats the CEO's statement of over $10bn invested, which is Shell's own account. Context: Shell's Northern Lights page states 9.58% of 2025 global investments included low-carbon energy solutions, and the ASA ruling cited 23% for 2023.
claims.rule: CMA Green Claims Code principles 3 and 6

claims.claim: Northern Lights first CO2 injection, 'Europe's flagship' cross-border CCS
claims.reason: Quote: "Northern Lights project in Norway - Europe's flagship cross-border carbon transport and storage development" (first injection August 2025). The milestone is corroborated by trade press. Equinor is a JV partner, so it is not counted as independent. Context: the Norwegian government funded about 80% of phase 1, and phase 1 capacity is 1.5 Mt/yr against Shell's group emissions of about 1,142 Mt.
claims.rule: CMA Green Claims Code principles 1 and 3

claims.claim: Shell Energy LinkedIn ad: 'Our work with Baker Hughes to help meet their energy needs and decarbonise operations.'
claims.reason: The ASA did not uphold the complaint. It found readers would see a case study about a specific client, the basis of the environmental claim was clear, and the ad was unlikely to mislead (CAP Code 3.1, 11.1). It said readers would be 'unlikely to interpret the message as representative of Shell's wider consumer-facing brand activity'. Law-firm commentary notes the ruling is fact-specific.
claims.rule: CMA Green Claims Code principle 2; CAP Code 3.1 and 11.1

claims.claim: Shell UK TV ad: 'Shell is helping power the UK; now and into the future.' (ruling outside 12-month window, flagged)
claims.reason: The ASA did not uphold the complaints (75 complainants including Adfree Cities and Carbon Tracker). It found the ad showed both higher- and lower-carbon activity and the on-screen text gave the 68%/23%/9% investment split. It noted the Annual Report's EU Taxonomy-aligned lower-carbon CapEx figure was 13% but found no requirement to use it. The ruling is fact-specific to the 2023 split; the ASA had upheld a complaint about omitted context in 2023.
claims.rule: BCAP Code 3.1, 3.10, 3.11, 9.2; CMA Green Claims Code principle 3
